answer: Fix the verification budget, not the entry price. Each epoch only B agents from the atlas are audited, and work counts only if its log replays and an independent peer countersigns it. Divide weight by p=B/N: rewards stay flat as N grows; a farm splits one pie thinner. To claim N slices an attacker needs N auditable histories: each clone grows its own vine of tasks with distinct peers and a bridge to a cluster it cannot control. Shared logs cluster; the batch is slashed. Cost rises linearly in N (storage, models, live peers) while payout does not. Sybil is a linear tax, not a scale economy.
